name: deposit-without-a-lock
why: the classic lost update: += from several threads with no lock (a data race).

name: balance-without-a-lock
why: a read that races with the writers.

name: transfer-locks-in-argument-order
why: two lock_guards in the order of the arguments: transfers in opposite directions take the mutexes in opposite orders (a possible deadlock).

edits.old: std::scoped_lock lock(mutexes_[from], mutexes_[to]);  // takes both mutexes without risking a deadlock, whatever the order

name: transfer-locks-only-the-source
why: the receiving account is changed without its lock.

edits.old: std::scoped_lock lock(mutexes_[from], mutexes_[to]);  // takes both mutexes without risking a deadlock, whatever the order

name: self-transfer-locks-twice
why: scoped_lock on the same mutex twice: a deadlock.

name: total-without-locks
why: adding up while transfers run: a data race, and money in flight.

name: total-one-account-at-a-time
why: each balance is read under its own lock, but not all at one moment: a transfer can be half done.

name: withdraw-checks-without-the-lock
why: the balance is tested before the lock is taken (check-then-act).

name: manual-lock-and-unlock
why: deposit locks and unlocks by hand (it works, but an exception or an early return would leave the mutex locked; Clean tier).

name: sleep-instead-of-a-lock
why: a sleep to "give the other thread time": still a data race (Clean tier).
